client: Hi Luna, lately I've been feeling really anxious about my job. Jessica, my colleague in the marketing firm, has been taking credit for my ideas, and it's making me feel undervalued. It’s hard not to feel like my contributions don’t matter, and I’m starting to worry about my job security. I’m not sure if talking about this will really help, though.
therapist:
Hi there! It sounds like you’re experiencing a lot of anxiety related to your job and feeling undervalued, especially with Jessica taking credit for your ideas. That can be incredibly frustrating and disheartening. I hear you saying that you’re not sure if talking about this will help, but I want to assure you that it’s completely valid to express these feelings.

You mentioned feeling like your contributions don’t matter, which can really affect your sense of security at work. I wonder if there’s a part of you that feels even more overwhelmed or hurt by this situation than you’re able to express right now. It’s okay to feel that way. Can we explore what this experience has been like for you a bit more? What do you think might be the biggest impact of Jessica’s actions on how you see yourself at work?
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, very quiet, very rapid speech

I wonder if there’s a part of you that feels more deeply affected by this situation than what you’ve shared so far. Sometimes, even just voicing our concerns can help clarify what we really want or need, without necessarily leading to conflict.
